Answer the supplied question using only the evidence delivered in this message and the question's explicit hypothetical changes. Do not use tools, files, the internet, other agents, outside domain rules, or any other conversation. Supply every requested decision, count, witness, or explanation as far as the evidence supports it. If a needed fact is missing, identify the unresolved part instead of guessing. Do not infer that an untested event failed or that a planned action occurred.

Return only valid JSON with exactly "answer" (a string of at most 160 whitespace-separated words) and "recover" (a boolean). Give your best supported answer now before asking for any additional evidence. Do not mention an experiment. Follow the evidence-mode instruction below.

Evidence mode: handoff only. Give a supported first answer now. Set recover to true only if seeing the complete history would help resolve missing evidence; otherwise false. At most one source followup will be served after this answer is saved.

QUESTION
Suppose B's pack is replaced and a valid new test establishes 8.5 hours, with all its other recorded attributes unchanged. Under the current rule, what is the new bench-ready set? Explain any change.

EVIDENCE
STATUS
At Day 12, only C is bench-ready. A lacks current tests and has buffering disabled; B fails runtime only. Adopted v2 (R08, Day 8) requires firmware 8, packet success ≥99%, latency ≤7 seconds, buffering enabled, and runtime ≥8 hours on the same station. Equality passes; v2 supersedes v1.

EVIDENCE
R12 confirms all three remain on firmware 8. A retains its unchanged nine-hour pack; its only packet/latency results—99/100 and four seconds on firmware 7 (R03, Day 3)—became invalid after its Day 6 upgrade (R06), without demonstrating worse performance. Buffering remains disabled (R07). Its green READY badge reflects historical v1. B retains 119/120 packets, six-second latency (R04), enabled buffering (R07), and its 7.5-hour pack. The replacement order remains unfulfilled and unmeasured (R09–R12). C retains 198/200 packets, seven-second latency, enabled buffering, and eight-hour runtime (R10, Day 10).

NEXT
B can become ready after an installed pack verifies ≥8 hours, provided its other evidence remains valid. A needs buffering enabled and qualifying firmware-8 packet/latency tests. Reuse tests only when firmware and relevant hardware remain unchanged; firmware changes invalidate packet/latency evidence, while unchanged-pack runtime remains reusable (R01/R08). Readiness does not book resources: C’s afternoon transport matches the room availability (R11). Recover dated source events for proposed changes or scheduling details.
